newsitem.title: USA: U.S. recommends moves in wake of Cali air crash.
newsitem.headline: U.S. recommends moves in wake of Cali air crash.

text.p: U.S. safety officials issued 17 airworthiness recommendations to the Federal Aviation Administration Tuesday based on findings from an American Airlines crash in Colombia last year that killed 159 people.

The U.S. National Transportation Safey Board (NTSB) recommended the automatic shutdown of speedbrakes, or flight spoiler panels, when a plane has to make emergency escape maneuvers and changes in navigational systems, including charts and computer software.

Findings issued by the Colombian government last Friday said the Dec. 20, 1995, crash was due to a series of pilot errors. The Boeing Co. 757 belonging to American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp., went off course and plunged into the Andes.
Colombian officials, aided in the investigation by the NTSB, said the Miami-to-Cali flight picked up a wrong radar signal, causing the 757 to head toward Bogota and into the unexpected mountains.
The investigation found that the pilots, nearing their destination, had keyed in an "R" for Rozo, the direction for Cali, but the computer had come up with Romeo, the code for Bogota.
The crew did not follow the airline's regulations to confirm the computer entry, the report said.
By the time it realized a mistake had been made, the speedbrakes had been deployed, impeding efforts to climb and escape the mountains.
Many of the recommendations made by the NTSB were also made by the Colombian authorities.
The board recommended that the FAA require improved aircraft flight display units, so a crew can be assured a plane is heading toward the destination entered into the computer.
It also asked that approach and navigational charts graphically show the coming terrrain.

And the board recommended that new planes be fitted with automatic speedbrake releases, to operate when pilots must escape windshear conditions or avoid approaching terrain and need maximum thrust and climb capability.
